festival.name: Latino Mar Bachata Festival
festival.tagline: Sea by day, club by night.
festival.description: Three days of bachata in Valencia. Workshops on the sand and in a seaside pavilion by day, socials with DJs, live acts and shows in a club by night. Beginners are welcome, and the Dominican roots of the dance are part of the programme.
themes: dancers from many countries in one city

tickets.name: Party Pass
includes: Entry to the Arena Stage, the pavilion practicas and Marea Club
tickets.notes: No workshops. Good for dancers who live in the city.

tickets.name: Group Full Pass (4 or more)
tickets.notes: Price per person. Book four or more passes together.

travel.title: By plane
travel.text: Fly to Valencia Airport. The metro runs from the airport to the city in about 25 minutes. A taxi to the beachfront takes about 25 minutes.

travel.title: By train
travel.text: High-speed trains arrive at the main station in the city centre. From there, the tram or a bus goes to the beachfront.

travel.title: Between venues
travel.text: All three venues are within a 15-minute walk of each other along the beachfront. The festival provides a signed walking route.

travel.title: By bike
travel.text: Valencia has a long coastal cycle path. Bikes can be parked next to the Arena Stage and Pabellón Brisa.

faq.question: Which workshop level should I pick?
faq.answer: Pick beginner if you have danced bachata fewer than ten times. Pick intermediate if you can dance a full song with turns. Pick advanced if you dance often and want to refine technique. The Which level am I? quiz on the Programme page helps you decide.

faq.question: Do I need a partner?
faq.answer: No. Workshops rotate partners, and every workshop has a role focus of lead, follow or both. Socials are open to everyone.

faq.question: What does the Full Pass include?
faq.answer: The Full Pass includes all workshops, all socials, all shows and entry to all three venues for the whole festival.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Wear light clothes for the day. Bring shoes you can dance in. For the sand, many dancers dance barefoot or in socks. Nights are warm, and the club has a cloakroom.

faq.question: Are the venues step-free?
faq.answer: Yes. All three venues have step-free access. See the Accessibility page for details on each venue, including quiet rooms and accessible toilets.

faq.question: When do the night socials end?
faq.answer: Friday and Saturday club socials run until 06:00 or earlier. The Sunday farewell night ends around 02:30. Check each set on the Programme page.

faq.question: How do I report a problem?
faq.answer: Tell any staff member wearing a Latino Mar T-shirt, or write to info@latinomar.example. All reports are handled in confidence. See the Code of conduct page.

faq.question: Can I transfer or cancel my pass?
faq.answer: You can transfer your pass to another person for free until 14 days before the festival. Cancellations are not refunded.

codeOfConduct.summary: Latino Mar is a place to dance, and everyone has the right to feel safe, respected and free to say no.
principles: Ask before you dance. A no is a complete answer, with or without a reason.
Respect your partner's boundaries on the dance floor, in dips and in close hold.
Leaders and followers are equal partners. Nobody has to dance with anyone.
No unwanted touching, comments or photos.
Look out for each other. Step in kindly if you see something wrong, or tell a staff member.
Respect all levels. Beginners are welcome, and teaching on the floor is for classes only unless asked.
Alcohol is not an excuse for crossing a boundary.

accessibility.summary: All three venues have step-free entrances, accessible toilets and a quiet space. This website is built to WCAG 2.0 AA.
features: Step-free access to Arena Stage, Pabellón Brisa and Marea Club
Quiet rooms at the pavilion and the club
Free ear protection at the club bar
Contact us before the festival if you have specific needs

sustainability.summary: The festival is held on a public beach. We keep the sea and the sand clean and cut waste where we can.
commitments: Reusable cups at every bar, with a small deposit
Free refill points for drinking water at all three venues
A recycling station at each venue and a beach clean-up on Sunday morning
Signed walking and cycling routes so you do not need a car
No single-use plastic bottles on sale

roots.intro: Bachata began in the Dominican Republic and has become one of the most danced Latin styles in the world. It grew in the barrios of Santo Domingo, where guitar-led songs about love and daily life were played at small parties.

timeline.text: The first bachata recordings are made in the Dominican Republic. They are commonly dated to this year.
Bachata grows in rural and working-class neighbourhoods. Many people look down on the music, and it is rarely played on the radio.
Bachata becomes popular across the country. Guitar styles evolve, and the music reaches a wider audience.
Modern bachata spreads worldwide. Dancers start to dance it in a close hold, and the sensual style emerges in Europe.
UNESCO inscribes bachata dominicana on its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

instruments.name: Requinto guitar
instruments.text: A lead guitar that plays the melody lines and gives bachata its bright, twanging sound.

instruments.name: Segunda guitar
instruments.text: A rhythm guitar that supports the lead guitar.

instruments.name: Bongo
instruments.text: A pair of small drums that mark the steady pulse the dancers follow.

instruments.name: Güira
instruments.text: A metal scraper that gives the rhythm its fine, scratchy texture.

instruments.name: Bass
instruments.text: Plays a simple repeating line under the guitars.

types.label: Social
types.description: Open dancing with a DJ or live music.

types.label: Show
types.description: A stage performance by a show team.

levels.label: Beginner
levels.description: You know the basic step or are new to bachata. You can dance part of a song with a partner.

levels.label: Intermediate
levels.description: You can dance a full song with turns and you feel the music.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.description: You dance often, lead or follow with confidence and want to refine technique.

levels.label: All levels
levels.description: Open to everyone. Used for socials, shows and relaxed classes.

styles.label: Bachata dominicana
styles.description: The traditional Dominican style with lively footwork.

styles.label: Bachata sensual
styles.description: A close, flowing style with body movement.

styles.label: Bachata moderna
styles.description: A modern style that mixes turns, musicality and open and close hold.

dayParts.label: Night (Club)
dayParts.description: Sessions that start at 20:00 or later.

venues.name: Arena Stage
venues.description: A sand-floor stage on the beachfront. It hosts the daytime sand workshops, the sunset socials and the open-air shows.

accessibility.notes: A firm boardwalk leads from the promenade to the edge of the dance floor. The sand floor itself is soft.

venues.name: Pabellón Brisa
venues.description: An air-conditioned seaside pavilion with a sprung wooden floor. It hosts most workshops, the evening practica socials and the pavilion showcases.

programmeItems.title: Welcome Practica: DJ Kiko Mar
programmeItems.description: DJ Kiko Mar plays bachata dominicana in the pavilion. A relaxed floor where beginners are welcome to join.

programmeItems.title: Welcome Sea Social: DJ Lorena Vela
programmeItems.description: DJ Lorena Vela plays bachata dominicana on the sand. Dance by the sea.

programmeItems.title: Your first bachata: the basic step
programmeItems.description: Start from zero. Learn the basic step in four counts, the side step and how to pause between songs. No partner needed.

programmeItems.title: Salsa on the sand: cross-body for bachata dancers
programmeItems.description: A relaxed all-levels class that borrows the cross-body lead from salsa and shows how it fits a bachata song.

programmeItems.title: Follow with ease: connection basics
programmeItems.description: Learn how to read a lead through the frame and the hand, and how to stay relaxed in a slow song.

programmeItems.title: Bachata on sand: balance and footwork
programmeItems.description: Sand changes how you step. Learn to keep your weight low, keep your steps small and stay balanced barefoot or in shoes.

programmeItems.title: Lead with ease: clear signals for beginners
programmeItems.description: Learn three simple lead signals, how to count the room and how to ask a stranger to dance.

programmeItems.title: Follower styling in the sea breeze
programmeItems.description: Add arm styling and soft body waves without losing your connection. For followers who know the basic step well.

programmeItems.title: Turn patterns that flow
programmeItems.description: Link three turn patterns without stopping. You work on timing, spotting and a quiet frame.

programmeItems.title: Leading spins without pulling
programmeItems.description: Learn to prepare, signal and release a spin with the frame, not the arm.

programmeItems.title: Slow musicality: dancing the pauses
programmeItems.description: Use silence, breaks and slow tempos. Explore how to listen first and move second.

programmeItems.title: Sunset steps: Dominican footwork for everyone
programmeItems.description: A sunset class on the roots of the dance: the side step, the tap and the small hip movement of traditional bachata.

programmeItems.title: Practica Social: DJ Tarek Noor
programmeItems.description: DJ Tarek Noor plays bachata moderna in the pavilion. A relaxed floor where beginners are welcome to join.
